summary: Elvana and Elvini: one state on two shores under a Speaker, the busiest fairs of the Sunhot realms and a loud, bloodless rivalry with Igara.

two_shores_speaker.name: The Speaker of Two Shores
two_shores_speaker.desc: Vinael speaks for Elvana and Elvini in one voice, in a hall built across the river mouth so that neither shore can say it was kept waiting. He is careful never to sit with his back to either.

union_endures.name: The Union Endures
union_endures.desc: The two shores keep the day they became one, with lanterns on the bridge and a feast on each bank. A child of Elvana weds a child of Elvini more often than not.

sun_fairs.name: The Sun Fairs
sun_fairs.desc: Fairs fill the market squares of both shores from thaw to harvest, and every Sunhot trader has a stall at one. A bargain struck at Elvana is honoured in every realm of the south.

merchant_houses.name: Merchant Houses of Elvana
merchant_houses.desc: The great houses of Elvana trade in sun-silk, spice and dyed wool, and keep agents in every Sunhot capital. Their ledgers are among the best in the south.

the_union_feast.title: The Union Feast
the_union_feast.desc: The two shores keep the day they became one council, with lanterns on the bridge and a feast on each bank. The Speaker is asked on which shore he will break the first loaf.

the_rival_at_igara.title: The Rival at Igara
the_rival_at_igara.desc: Igara's merchants sell sun-silk below our price again, and the guild-halls of Elvana buzz with complaint. The Speaker is asked to say whether to lower our prices or to carry the complaint to the Council.

elvana_asks_the_king_to_judge.title: Elvana Asks the King to Judge
elvana_asks_the_king_to_judge.desc: A letter arrives from Elvana in the Speaker's hand, courteous and brief. Elvana and Igara have quarrelled over prices for as long as the oldest merchants can remember, and Elvana asks the King of Gala to judge between them.

options.name: The King will speak for peace between them

pilgrims_on_the_sea_of_gods.title: Pilgrims on the Sea of Gods
pilgrims_on_the_sea_of_gods.desc: White sails carry pilgrims along the coast for the summer feasts. The harbour keeper of [ROOT.GetName] asks whether they are to be given moorings and a feast-day, or left to sail on.

focuses.name: Elvana and Elvini
focuses.desc: Elvana is one state on two shores: the old towns of Elvana and Elvini, united under one council. Its fairs are the busiest of the Sunhot realms, and its merchants' great rival is Igara next door.

focuses.name: The Speaker of Two Shores
focuses.desc: Vinael is the Speaker of both shores, and the only man trusted by both. He holds the office by a vote of two councils and the goodwill of a bridge.

focuses.name: The Union Feast
focuses.desc: Every year the two shores keep the day they became one, with lanterns on the bridge and a feast on each bank. Neither shore will be the first to leave the table.

focuses.name: Elvini Remembers
focuses.desc: Elvini keeps its own archive, and its scholars remember what the union cost them. The Speaker visits the archive and leaves a gift.

focuses.name: One Council, Two Shores
focuses.desc: The single council seats equal delegates from each shore, with a bench at the middle for the Speaker. Debates are conducted in turn, and neither shore interrupts.

focuses.name: The Union Endures
focuses.desc: The union is renewed in an oath on the bridge, sworn by both shores at once. The words are the same on each side, and are heard on the other.

focuses.name: The Markets of Elvana
focuses.desc: Elvana's squares are filled with stalls from dawn, and its warehouses stretch along the river. A new covered market is raised on the oldest square.

focuses.name: The Rival at Igara
focuses.desc: Igara is next door, and its merchants undercut every price in the south. The rivalry is old, loud and bloodless, and the Noon Council is tired of hearing about it.

focuses.name: The Sun Fairs
focuses.desc: The great fairs of Elvana draw traders from every Sunhot realm, and the stalls fill the squares on both shores. The Speaker opens each fair by lighting a lamp.

focuses.name: Undercut Igara
focuses.desc: The guild-halls vote to cut their prices to beat Igara's, and the Speaker lets them. The market is sharper, the rivalry is sourer, and the Council is displeased.

focuses.name: A Fair Market With Igara
focuses.desc: Elvana proposes a fair market with Igara: shared weights, shared dues and a common bench for disputes. The Council is pleased, and Igara, to its surprise, agrees.

focuses.name: Ask Gala to Judge
focuses.desc: If Elvana and Igara cannot agree, the King of Gala might judge between them. A letter is written, sealed and sent south.

focuses.name: Merchant Houses of Elvana
focuses.desc: The great merchant houses of Elvana set up counting-halls on both shores, and their agents travel to every Sunhot capital. A bargain struck at their tables is honoured everywhere.

focuses.name: The First Market of the Sun
focuses.desc: Elvana's squares are now the first market of the Lands of the Sun, and its merchants quote their prices as the measure of every other. The Speaker lights the lamp himself.
